closest_three_official_comparators.actual: Wrap thin PTFE tape on fixed pipe thread in correct winding direction and coverage, tear and press tail. Disclosed material model derives deposited tape from relative angle/pay-out with tension.
closest_three_official_comparators.distinction: A preformed protective spring-like helix is expanded/wound around a branched flexible bundle, with no adhesive/seal, torn tail or fixed rigid thread. secondary_harness_leads: The four surfaced harness cases#464/#241/#210/#24 were now source-and-public-state checked; see bounded_harness_addendum. They are not generic unknown active ownership gaps. Other private/unindexed/newer-reference gaps remain.
actual_new_manipulation: Progressively expand/open/wind a preformed continuous helical sleeve around already grouped flexible wires, admitting actual branches while retaining the bundle and full required joint slack. This differs from closing a discrete carrier latch or simply routing a cable into a path.
physical_success_measurement: Use marked source-bound bundle span and visible branch/end landmarks, photos/ruler to show the intended wires remain physically encompassed by real sleeve after release; keep real attachment/service loop and manually sweep the intended joint through its declared normal range without taut wire, pullout, pinching or sleeve migration. Exact coverage, minimum bend/slack and proof-force thresholds remain to bind. No arbitrary zero-gap rule: a spiral sleeve naturally has pitch gaps. Wrong wire excluded, sleeve merely adjacent, prewrapped coil, pinned bundle or shortened fake loop must fail. Honest partial credit can measure retained correctly wrapped span, subject to branch/strain-relief integrity.
implementation_approach_for_later_planni: Real precurved open-helix rod/segmented sleeve with calibrated radial opening, bending/torsion and friction over actual cable bundle; preserve branch passage and physical enclosure/contact. Disclosed bounded compliant approximations allowed. Do not add snapping crossbar, adhesive tape or goal-triggered attachment. Use actual robot subassembly/start state as documented; no generic stand removing moving-joint requirement. Simulator-state expert planning is allowed. No task code was written.
implementation_complexity: Medium/high and uncertain: thin-sleeve grip, springback, multiple cable contact and full-span regrasp matter more than body count. Lower hidden-path/fill burden than ECHO full internal coil, but no measured cost claim. Not selected as a fastest rigid task.
potential_YAM_obstacles: Stock fingertip access under wrap and beside arm rail, regrasp while sleeve springs back, lateral holding of bundle, true full loop reach and attachment clearance. Nominal94mm aperture/50N configuration do not prove grip/contact. Full palm/wrist envelope must be overlaid after real geometry is bound.
cheap_disqualification_tests: First bind7378K43 current compatible part drawing/material and actual source robot span/branches. Stop if source turns out to be a different sleeve or the central wrap is already held by an earlier task.

With existing/sample component only if available, test a short local engagement through the genuine branch and stock-finger envelope; measure opening force/slip/retention and inverted/omitted-wire controls. This is an early kill coupon, not full-task proof.
Check whole real span, attachments and normal arm/grabber sweep. Stop if only enlarged sleeve/fake handles, deleted arm obstruction, tied-in-place cable or shortened loop makes it work.

Before implementation GO, show simple physical inspection/sweep distinguishes correct wrapping from sleeve laying nearby, misplaced branch and insufficient slack. No need to demand completed GPU/hardware demonstration merely for deep-dive screen PASS.
strongest_likely_reviewer_rejection: This could be ordinary cable dressing already covered by#1916/#17, with robot importance borrowed from a story. A generic self-attaching coil around rigid rods would remove the actual sheath interface and motion slack. The defense must retain true open-helix wrapping, genuine robot branch topology and moving-joint functional endpoint; no claim that the guide alone resolves catalogue dimensions, ownership or robot feasibility.

new_public_PR_reads.title: Lay a robot axis's two cables into its cable carrier and snap every crossbar shut by AMMistry18 · Pull Request #1916 · robocurve/benchmark-tasks · GitHub
comments: The robot fills a robot axis's cable carrier, a step in building every linear axis or gantry for a robot cell. Two limp cables (grey motor, orange encoder), clamped in the strain relief at the fixed end, must be laid side by side into a real-size igus E2 mini carrier (12 links, 25 mm inner width), grey on the far side and never crossing. Each of the 12 hinged crossbars must then be swung over and pressed until its sprung catch snaps over it. One hand lifts each cable over the side plates near the fixed end while the other lays its far end. A crossbar resting on its catch, or shut on a cable riding a side plate, does not count. new_public_PR_reads.title: Add task: Wrap a pipe thread with thread-seal tape from a dispenser, the way the fitting turns on by DarK404 · Pull Request #1465 · robocurve/benchmark-tasks · GitHub
comments: Adds tasks/wrap-a-pipe-thread-with-thread-seal-tape-from-a-dispenser-the-way-the-fitting-turns-on/ . A 3/4-inch pipe nipple stands upright in a floor flange, its male thread at the top, and a handheld PTFE tape dispenser lies on a mat beside it. The robot must wrap the thread, ready for a fitting to be screwed on, and put the dispenser back. The instruction does not state the trade standard that is scored: wound the way the fitting turns on (clockwise seen from the thread's end; wound the other way the tape bunches and the joint leaks), 3 to 6 turns covering the thread with the first thread left bare, torn off and its tail pressed down. PhysX has no tape, so it is our own model: the tape is wound by the roll's path round the pipe, comes off only as the roll turns on the dispenser's braked spindle (a PhysX hinge), and its stretch pulls the roll round; a steady wrap pays out at 0.2 to 0.6 N, and a yank outruns the braked roll and tears the tape at 1.5 N. Scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (success at step 609 of 1,600; four turns clockwise, the thread covered, the tail pressed down by the second hand) Media: M-4KYK3E Shortcut checks ( TAPE_DEMO=backwards , TAPE_DEMO=nopress ): the same wrap anticlockwise scores 0; the tail left standing scores 0.5 Offline checks of the tape model (including that a roll which cannot turn tears the tape in its first turn), every scoring tier, and the demo's reach and per-step limits: python -m pytest -q test_tape_wrap.py (33 tests) 🤖 Generated with Claude Code
